assertion.statement: For known simple-zero ring instances with fixed E,pi,old local types and omega(k)≤A, the actual primitive class-functional coordinate has v2 at least−C(E,A), independently of the active support and companion field.
assertion.objects: The actual primitive coordinates and bounded minimal two-term models, their primitive generic-kernel vectors, the outer DVR and derivative-switch sequence.
assertion.hypotheses: Nonzero actual central class with bounded nonzero calibration multiplier gives generic rank1; bounded residual models and outer evaluation are supplied. Nonquadratic outer rank-two detection, exact annihilator duality and actual-class determinant switch preservation hold. The paired functional has fixed denominator exponent a.
assertion.quantifiers: Every known simple-zero ring instance under the stated fixed data and companion-prime count bound.
assertion.parameter_range: Outer contradiction sequence with omega(k_j)≤A; each construction uses only finitely many switches.
assertion.uniformity: C depends on E,A and the fixed old data, not active support or varying companion field. No bound uniform in arbitrarily many switches is used.
assertion.constants: At terminal outer rank1 a nonzero minor has one finite valuation b on an outer-large set and gives v2(u_j)≥−a−b; this contradicts a sequence tending to−infinity.
assertion.normalizations: Primitive vectors select localizations; the actual inner classes and their own paired functionals determine the preserved coordinates. Terminal formula is ±alpha beta/Delta with alpha integral and v2(beta)≥−a.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No uniform numerical bound at the unknown full-corank-one base. Bounded matrix size alone is insufficient; the proof uses nonzero class, detection and determinant-preserving switches.
assertion.limit_order: Assume a countersequence; fix bounded model size on an outer-large set; reduce outer kernel dimension by finite switches while preserving inner valuations; choose a nonzero terminal minor and contradict unbounded negative valuation.
